ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a white right triangle, with the horizontal base labeled 6, a vertical side on the right, and the hypotenuse labeled 10; the problem states that 10 only represents the hypotenuse of this white triangle. The gray shaded region is on the right, with the horizontal width of the base labeled 3, the left and right sides are vertical lines, and the upper side is the extension of the same slanted line. Then reason: the height of the white right triangle is sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(64) = 8. The rise/horizontal distance corresponding to the slope of the slanted line is 8/6 = 4/3. The horizontal width of the shaded part is 3, so the height on the right side is greater than the height on the left side by (4/3)*3 = 4, that is, the height on the right side is 8 + 4 = 12. The shaded region can be regarded as a trapezoid whose vertical parallel sides are respectively 8 and 12 and whose distance between them is 3, and the area is (1/2)(8 + 12)(3) = 30.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a white right triangle on the left with horizontal leg 6, vertical leg unknown, and its slanted hypotenuse labeled 10; the shaded region to the right has horizontal width 3, vertical sides, and its upper slanted edge is the continuation of the same slanted line. Use the text note to treat 10 as only the hypotenuse of the white triangle. Compute the white triangle height by Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(10^2-6^2)=8. Since the same slanted line continues, use similar triangles/slope: the rise per run is 8/6=4/3, so over the shaded width 3 the height increases by 4, making the right vertical height 12. Then view the shaded region as a trapezoid with parallel vertical sides 8 and 12 separated by distance 3, and compute area = (1/2)(8+12)(3)=30.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a large right triangle whose base is split into lengths 6 and 3, with a vertical segment at the split creating the white right triangle; the shaded part is the portion between that vertical segment and the right vertical side. Use the text note that the 10 belongs to the white triangle’s hypotenuse only. First find the height of the white triangle from legs 6 and hypotenuse 10: height 8. The entire large triangle has base 6+3=9 and is similar to the white triangle because both are right triangles sharing the same slanted side angle. Thus its height is scaled by 9/6, giving total right-side height 8*(9/6)=12. Find the shaded area as large triangle area minus white triangle area: (1/2)(9)(12) - (1/2)(6)(8) = 54 - 24 = 30.
